plan.title: Aldosterone vs vehicle kidney: DE, pathways, TF activity
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 human kidney bulk RNA-seq samples (6 aldosterone-treated, 6 vehicle control), unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon gene-level counts across 12,000 genes. The research question asks which transcription factors drive the treated-vs-control response, ranked to the top 6 per direction. The plan follows the Inflexa-grounded bulk RNA-seq procedure end to end: (1) sample-structure QC on variance-stabilized counts to confirm the samples separate by condition and there is no outlier/batch structure before any test is trusted; (2) minimal low-count pre-filtering (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size) followed by PyDESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization built into the model, a Wald test with an explicit reference level (vehicle) and a named contrast (condition: aldosterone vs vehicle), apeglm-style shrinkage of the reported fold changes, and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with independent filtering at alpha=0.05; (3) two downstream interpretive layers computed off the same DE contrast statistic — a preranked GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark (with Reactome and WikiPathways as follow-up collections, all present in the reference store) for pathway context, and a decoupleR ulm transcription-factor activity inference on the CollecTRI human regulon network (with DoRothEA confidence A-C as an alternative check), which directly answers the research question by scoring every regulator's inferred activity change and letting us report the top 6 activated and top 6 repressed TFs; (4) a final consolidated report that ties the DE results, the TF activities, and the pathway enrichment together with full reproducibility metadata. Every script is Python per the user's constraint (PyDESeq2, decoupler, gseapy), and every reference (CollecTRI, DoRothEA, MSigDB Hallmark/Reactome/WikiPathways) is confirmed present in the environment before being named. With only 6 per group, single-batch, no covariates, this design is squarely in the range the DESeq2/PyDESeq2 Wald + BH procedure is grounded for; no robustness cross-check with edgeR is included because the environment's Python-only constraint and the available R edgeR track are not being mixed here, but the DoRothEA-vs-CollecTRI TF comparison serves as the internal robustness check for the central TF-activity question.

decoupler ulm on CollecTRI human regulons using the Wald statistic of all tested genes
